title: Slim the /sdlc skill to run+report+HITL; harden supervision + long-haul monitoring (PRs B, C, D of #3364)
summary: Task decomposition for the three remaining, mutually-independent PRs of #3364 (PR A already landed via #3421 — do not redo). Three parallel slices, one PR each, disjoint file sets so no integration collision: slice-B (long-haul monitoring tooling: bin/wait-status filter flags + a new slice.closed EventType, additive/low-risk), slice-C (supervision hardening in JobSupervisor/supervision_policy.py: rate-limit classification distinct from abnormal, windowed paced retry preserving landed slices, deterministic-loop guard, behavioral/medium-high risk), slice-D (slim SKILL.md + remove overseer_owns_host_detection, deletion/medium risk, GATED on an internal coverage-map). The architect owns the technical design/DAG and the classifier/window mechanics; this artifact owns the per-slice task decomposition, intra-slice ordering, the PR-D internal gate, and PR packaging. Grounded live against main @ ca193b85b on 2026-07-06; all refiner anchors re-verified (see grounding). cq-1 is resolved: PR C paced-retry has NO hard wall-clock ceiling but MUST emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold. The PR-D coverage-map is genuine verification work, not a rubber stamp: the live overseer monitor emits a DIFFERENT deterministic vocabulary (post_consensus_stall, incomplete_consensus_stall, rerun_anomaly, status_inconsistency, hitl_propagation_failure, cross_phase_inconsistency, orchestrator_unreachable) plus LLM-classifier action:{action} alerts — there is NO deterministic emitter for agent-stall / agent-silent / agent-nack-unresolved / phase-long-running, so each deleted block must be positively mapped to an emitter (structural OR classifier path) before deletion; any block with no confirmed emitter is raised as a HITL at point of discovery, not silently deleted into a dark gap.

scope_notes.in_scope: PRs B, C, D as three independent slices / units with separate risk profiles; one PR per slice.
out_of_scope: PR A (issue item 5) — landed via #3421 (CONSENSUS_TIMEOUT_RETRY_OPTION → restart_phase in orchestrator/routes/decisions/_handlers.py). Do not touch.
The 13 visibility-gap follow-ups from the issue comments (per-role commits_ahead, consensus-window countdown, alert feed, …) — tracked in #3369 / #3499 / #3508 / #3509.
Item 2 liveness-before-destructive gating — largely landed (#3341 via #3343); the skill keeps only a thin backstop rule, it is NOT re-implemented here.
scope_notes.independence: B, C, D touch disjoint file sets (B: bin/wait-status + events.py + slice_scheduler.py + routes/pipelines; C: supervision_policy.py + auth_errors.py + concurrent_executor.py; D: SKILL.md + models/_config.py + routes/pipelines/_routes_status.py). No shared file → true parallel slices, NOT a linear dependency chain. Only within slice-D is there an intra-slice gate (coverage-map before deletion).
scope_notes.cq1_resolution: PR C paced-retry bounds itself with NO hard wall-clock ceiling (retry until the cap lifts) BUT emits an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold, so an attended operator is informed while auto-recovery continues. Applies to task-C-2/task-C-4.

approach.slicing: Three independent slices = three PRs. Each slice is self-contained and green (make lint + make test) on its own branch. No cross-slice ordering constraint; they may proceed in parallel.
approach.pr_b_strategy: Additive only. Flags are client-side JSON-line filtering in the launcher (no new imports). slice.closed is a new EventType emitted at both scheduler close sites with a payload that distinguishes success vs failure and names the slice, then allowlisted so it reaches /status/wait consumers. Regression-guard the existing flags + default output.
approach.pr_c_strategy: New transient-rate-limit classification that keys off the all-producers agent-invocation-failure streak signature carrying the throttling wording auth_errors deliberately excludes (429/'rate limit'/'overloaded'). On that classification: windowed paced retry across the rolling cap window (hours-scale, parse reset time from the error when present else bounded backoff, NO hard ceiling per cq-1), using a restart_phase-equivalent that PRESERVES landed slices; emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold (cq-1); and a deterministic-loop guard that escalates instead of looping when a restart reproduces the identical failure signature at the same phase-progression point. Genuinely-fatal auth (EX_AUTH_FATAL incl. matched weekly caps) and ordinary abnormal paths stay unchanged. Highest test burden — see risks.
approach.pr_d_strategy: GATED deletion. task-D-1 produces the per-block coverage-map FIRST and is a hard predecessor of the deletion tasks; if any block lacks a confirmed overseer emitter, raise a HITL (mcp__sdlc__register_open_question) at point of discovery rather than deleting into a dark gap. Then delete the five host-detector blocks + migration section + Overseer-Absent Fallback + Stuck-Pipeline-Rescue host trigger + short-flow Stall block, PRESERVING the render-on-OVERSEER_ALERT paths (Long-Running Implement Phase + Unresolved NACK AskUserQuestion flows). Remove overseer_owns_host_detection entirely (field + both refs, grep clean). Add a short last-resort debugging section with the two thin backstops.

phases.name: PR B — Long-haul monitoring tooling (issue items 3+4): bin/wait-status filter flags + slice.closed event
phases.pr: one PR; additive only; no behavior change to existing flags or default output

tasks.description: Add --exclude-types (comma-separated event-type filter that drops matching JSON lines client-side) and --quiet flags to skills/sdlc/bin/wait-status. Filtering is purely client-side on the emitted JSON lines; keep the launcher pure-stdlib and self-contained (no new imports/deps). Wire the flags into the existing render/emit loop alongside the current --since/--inner-timeout/--max-iterations args.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-B1: both flags present and functional; --exclude-types drops lines whose event type matches; --quiet suppresses per-line noise per its documented behavior; no new imports. AC-B2: existing --since/--inner-timeout/--max-iterations behavior and the non-filtered default output are byte-for-byte unchanged.

tasks.description: Add a slice.closed member to the EventType StrEnum (orchestrator/events.py) and emit it at BOTH SliceScheduler.record_complete (slice_scheduler.py:361) and record_failure (:371). The event payload must carry enough to (a) identify the slice (slice_id) and (b) distinguish success vs failure (e.g. an outcome/status field), so a consumer can tell a completion from a failure without a second lookup.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-B3: slice.closed EventType exists; exactly one slice.closed emitted at record_complete and one at record_failure; payload identifies the slice and distinguishes success vs failure.

tasks.description: Add slice.closed to the _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES allowlist (orchestrator/routes/pipelines/__init__.py:405) so it passes the /status/wait allowlist check (_routes_status.py:349) and reaches wait-status consumers.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-B4: slice.closed is in _STATUS_WAIT_EVENT_TYPES; a slice.closed event is not filtered out by the /status/wait allowlist.

tasks.description: Tests: (a) --exclude-types drops a targeted event type and --quiet behaves per spec, while default output is unchanged (regression guard for AC-B2); (b) a slice completion emits exactly one allowlisted slice.closed(success) and a slice failure emits exactly one allowlisted slice.closed(failure). Run make lint + make test green.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-B5: tests cover both new flags (drop-a-type + quiet) and both emit sites (completion and failure each emit exactly one allowlisted slice.closed distinguishable by outcome). Suite green.

phases.name: PR C — Supervision hardening (issue items 1+6): rate-limit classification, windowed paced retry, deterministic-loop guard
phases.pr: one PR; live supervision behavior; heavy test coverage over classification + loop-guard + landed-slice preservation

tasks.description: Add a transient rate-limit / cap-wall classification DISTINCT from abnormal. Detect the all-producers agent-invocation-failure streak signature whose underlying error carries the throttling wording auth_errors.py deliberately excludes from EX_AUTH_FATAL (bare 429 / 'rate limit' / 'overloaded'), and classify it as transient rate-limit rather than routing it into the agent-invocation-fail-streak halt. Reuse/extend the auth_errors throttling-signature vocabulary rather than duplicating regexes; do NOT widen EX_AUTH_FATAL. Keep genuinely-fatal auth (matched weekly/usage caps) and ordinary abnormal untouched.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-C1: the throttling-streak signature is classified as transient rate-limit, not abnormal, and does not trip the fail-streak halt. AC-C6 (partial): EX_AUTH_FATAL matches (incl. weekly caps) and non-throttling abnormal failures classify exactly as before.

tasks.description: On the transient rate-limit classification, perform a windowed paced retry across the rolling cap window (hours-scale, NOT the 30s SUPERVISION_BACKOFF_CAP_SECONDS) without hammering the API: parse the reset time from the error when present to pace, else bounded backoff. Per resolved cq-1: NO hard wall-clock ceiling (retry until the cap lifts), BUT emit an OVERSEER_ALERT once the wait crosses a threshold so an attended operator is informed while auto-recovery continues.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-C2: paced retry runs on the hours-scale cap window without hammering (reset-time-paced when available, else bounded backoff). AC-C5: bounding/escalation matches cq-1 — no hard ceiling AND an OVERSEER_ALERT fires once the wait crosses the threshold.

tasks.description: Make the paced retry use a restart_phase-equivalent that PRESERVES landed slices — completed slice work must NOT be discarded on recovery. Reuse the existing restart_phase machinery / slice-completion state rather than a full cold restart.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-C3: after a rate-limit paced restart, previously-completed slices remain complete (not re-run / not discarded).

tasks.description: Add a deterministic-loop guard that distinguishes transient from deterministic failure: if a restart reproduces the IDENTICAL failure signature at the SAME phase-progression point (no state advance), STOP and escalate (HITL/halt) instead of looping; if the restart advances state, continue the paced-retry policy. Guard against infinite paced loops.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-C4: an identical-failure-at-same-point reproduction escalates and stops looping; a restart that advances state continues.

tasks.description: Tests: throttling-streak → rate-limit classification (asserting it is NOT abnormal and does not trip the fail-streak halt); paced-retry pacing/window (hours-scale, reset-time-paced vs bounded backoff; OVERSEER_ALERT fires past threshold per cq-1); landed-slice preservation across a paced restart; loop-guard escalates on identical-failure reproduction and continues when state advances; regression: EX_AUTH_FATAL (incl. weekly cap) and ordinary abnormal halts still fire unchanged (AC-C6). Run make lint + make test green.
tasks.acceptance_criteria: AC-C7 + AC-C6: all above cases covered and green; existing fatal/abnormal halts asserted unchanged.

non_goals: Re-implementing liveness-before-destructive gating (#3341/#3343) — only a thin backstop rule is kept.
Adding NEW overseer detectors to fill a parity gap — that is an operator decision raised as HITL if task-D-1 finds a gap, not pre-scoped here.
risks_for_reviewers: PR C is the highest-risk slice (live supervision behavior). The rate-limit classification must key ONLY off the throttling-streak signature; a too-broad match would swallow genuine abnormal halts (AC-C6 regression). Reviewers: confirm EX_AUTH_FATAL and abnormal paths are provably untouched.

PR C loop-guard correctness: 'identical failure at the same point' needs a concrete signature (error class + phase-progression marker). A weak signature either loops forever (transient mislabeled deterministic-safe) or escalates prematurely. Heavy tests both directions (AC-C7).

PR C cq-1: NO hard ceiling means an unattended pipeline can sit paused for days on a weekly cap; the OVERSEER_ALERT-past-threshold is the ONLY operator signal — it must actually fire. Do not silently add a ceiling.

PR D task-D-1 is a genuine gate, not a formality: there is NO deterministic emitter for agent-stall/agent-silent/agent-nack-unresolved/phase-long-running (only the LLM classifier action:{action} path). If a block maps only to the classifier path, that is still an emitter the skill surfaces — but reviewers must confirm the skill's alert-surfacing actually renders it; where nothing maps, it MUST be a HITL, not a delete.
PR D task-D-2 must not over-delete: the Stuck Pipeline Rescue workflow Steps 1-3 and the two AskUserQuestion render-on-alert flows STAY (AC-D3/AC-D4). Only host-side detection triggers go.
PR B slice.closed payload must be distinguishable success vs failure at emit time (single event type, outcome field) — a consumer should not need a second lookup to tell a completion from a failure.

ordering.cross_slice: None. B, C, D are independent (disjoint file sets) and may proceed in parallel; each lands as its own PR.
ordering.intra_slice_B: task-B-2 (EventType + emit) → task-B-3 (allowlist) can be co-authored; task-B-1 (flags) independent; task-B-4 tests last.
ordering.intra_slice_C: task-C-1 (classify) → task-C-2 (paced retry) → task-C-3 (preserve slices) → task-C-4 (loop guard) → task-C-5 (tests). Roughly sequential (each builds on the classification hook).
ordering.intra_slice_D: task-D-1 (coverage-map GATE) is a HARD predecessor of task-D-2 (SKILL.md deletion) and task-D-3 (config removal). task-D-4/D-5 (kept-surface + verification) follow the deletions.
ordering.risk_priority: C highest (behavioral), D medium (gated deletion), B low (additive). Prefer landing B first for quick value; C and D independent.
